Validation of the Turkish version of the artificial intelligence attitude in radiology scale for patients.
desc: [Work (Reading, Mass.)] BackgroundIn the context of the growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into radiology, AI-assisted systems are increasingly presented as tools for improving diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and clinical decision-making. Yet discussions of AI in radiology often focus on technical performance or clinician perspectives, while patients' attitudes toward these technologies remain less well understood.ObjectiveThis study aimed to cross-culturally adapt the Artificial Intelligence Attitude in Radiology Scale (AIARS) for patients into Turkish and evaluate the psychometric properties of the modified Turkish version among patients receiving radiology services.MethodsThis cross-sectional validation study included 659 adult patients aged 18-69 years (Mage = 34.50, SD = 11.21). The factor structure was examined using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Measurement invariance was tested across age groups, gender, and educational level using multi-group CFA.ResultsEFA supported a modified four-factor, 23-item structure derived from the original 39-item, five-factor AIARS. CFA confirmed that the four-factor model was a good fit for the data, χ2(224) = 640.16, p < .001, CFI = .985, TLI = .983, RMSEA = .075, 90% CI [.068, .082], SRMR = .072. The total scale demonstrated high internal consistency, with α = .87 and ω = .88. Test-retest reliability was excellent (total-scale ICC = .97, 95% CI [.94, .99]). Measurement invariance was supported across age, gender, and educational level.ConclusionThe modified Turkish version of the AIARS demonstrated acceptable psychometric performance at the total-scale level and may be used to assess patients' attitudes toward AI in radiology. However, the Worries and Ethical Concerns factor requires further evaluation.

title: First POC Active Syphilis Test FDA Authorization
Use of a large language model for identification and extraction of actionable details from recommendations for additional imaging in abdominopelvic CT reports.
desc: [Abdominal radiology (New York)] Automated identification and extraction of recommendations for additional imaging (RAI) from radiology reports could facilitate closed-loop tracking and follow-up completion. We compare a prompt-engineered GPT-4.1 large language model (LLM) versus a validated encoder-only transformer deep learning model (bidirectional encoder representations from transformers [BERT]) for detection of RAI in abdominopelvic computed tomography (CTAP) reports, and evaluate GPT-4.1 for extraction of actionable RAI elements. This retrospective study included CTAP reports from a multi-institution system in 2023. LLM and BERT were used to identify RAI from radiology reports; LLM also extracted RAI actionable elements (modality, body part, time frame, rationale). Recall, precision, F1, and accuracy for RAI detection were determined using human-annotated reference standard. Paired comparison between each model's accuracy used McNemar's test. LLM recall, precision, F1, and accuracy for actionable element extraction were computed. Element prevalence was compared using chi-square test. 2000 random reports for unique patients (58% women; mean age 58.5 ± 17.5) included 215 RAI within 206 reports. For RAI detection, GPT-4.1 recall, precision, F1 and accuracy were 95.6%, 98.5%, 97.0% and 99.4%, respectively; BERT recall, precision, F1 and accuracy were 93.7%, 96.5%, 95.1% and 99.0% (p = 0.16). Recommendation element recall were as follows: 100.0% for time frame, 93.9% for body part, 90.2% for rationale, and 94.2% for modality. Precision were 100.0%, 95.7%, 94.6% and 86.1%, respectively. 29/215 (13.5%) RAI were complete (specified all actionable elements). Prevalence of actionable elements varied (p < 0.001), highest for rationale (215/215, 100%), followed by body part (213/215, 99.1%), modality (191/215, 88.8%), and time frame (31/215, 14.4%). GPT-4.1 demonstrated high accuracy for extraction of RAI and enabled accurate extraction of actionable elements. LLM integration into radiology workflows can facilitate automatic closed-loop communication and tracking of recommended imaging, which may reduce diagnostic delays.

title: A Comparative Usability Study of Three AI Interpretation Tools in Simulated ICU Family Meetings.
desc: [Applied clinical informatics] Background Effective communication in the ICU is essential, yet timely access to professional interpreters remains challenging for patients with non-English language preference. Language discordance in high-acuity settings has been associated with miscommunication, delays in care, and adverse outcomes. Speech-based artificial intelligence (AI) interpretation tools have emerged as potential adjuncts to bridge communication gaps, but comparative usability data in high-stakes clinical settings remain limited. Objective To evaluate and compare clinician-reported usability of three speech-based AI interpretation tools during physician-led simulated ICU family meetings. Methods We conducted a comparative study involving 21 ICU physicians. Each participant completed three simulated ICU family meetings representing high-stakes scenarios including ECMO discussion, tracheotomy planning, and transition to comfort care. Participants were assigned to one non-English language (Spanish, Chinese, or Arabic) and used three speech-based interpretation tools (AI-TransLATE, ChatGPT, and Gemini) in counterbalanced order. After each encounter, clinicians completed the System Usability Scale (SUS) and structured Likert-scale assessments of satisfaction, perceived communication effectiveness, effort, and acceptability. Results AI-TransLATE achieved a median SUS of 70.0 (IQR 64.4-75.6) and ChatGPT 72.5 (IQR 70.0- 75.0), both meeting the acceptable threshold (≥70). Gemini received 40.0 (IQR 25.0-57.5), falling below the acceptable range. Gemini differed significantly from both AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT, while AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT did not differ significantly. Satisfaction, perceived communication effectiveness, and willingness to use in clinical practice were also significantly higher for AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT compared with Gemini. Conclusion In simulated ICU family meetings, select speech-based AI interpretation tools demonstrated acceptable clinician-reported usability, supporting further investigation of their potential as complementary interpretation tools when professional interpreter access is limited. Future work should prioritize validation and evaluation of patient understanding in real-world settings , to support safe and scalable implementation.

title: Regulation of medical artificial intelligence in public health: governance lessons and implications for China.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] With the deep integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into public health and clinical care, challenges including dynamic algorithm iteration, data security risks, and ambiguous liability allocation pose multifaceted threats to traditional regulatory frameworks. Among these challenges, this study focuses specifically on the tension between static pre-market approval and the continuous iteration of AI-enabled medical systems. Globally, the European Union (EU), the United States (US), and Japan have developed distinct regulatory models that offer valuable lessons for China. This paper conducts a comparative analysis of medical AI regulatory logics and institutional practices across jurisdictions, with particular attention to algorithm modification, lifecycle oversight, and continuous post-market evaluation. Building on international experience, we propose an optimized institutional pathway for China that centers on differentiated algorithm-change control, continuous lifecycle evaluation, and risk-based regulatory adjustment, while treating liability allocation, risk classification, and data governance as supporting dimensions. This framework provides theoretical support and practical guidance for improving China's medical AI regulatory system, promoting standardized technology development, and supporting the orderly development of public health services in the digital health era.

title: An Integrated Systems Biology and Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Robust Placental Biomarker Discovery in Preeclampsia.
source: PubMed · FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
desc: [FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology] Preeclampsia (PE) is a heterogeneous pregnancy disorder characterized by placental dysfunction and immune dysregulation. Translation of transcriptomic biomarkers has been limited by inconsistent feature selection, inadequate external validation, and poor model interpretability. We developed an explainable, externally validated, transcriptomics-driven artificial intelligence framework for biomarker discovery, PE diagnosis, and exploratory severity stratification. Placental transcriptomic datasets were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were integrated with consensus feature selection using Elastic Net, LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Boruta. Selected biomarkers were evaluated using conventional machine learning, deep learning, ensemble, and hybrid models with repeated stratified cross-validation and independent cross-platform external validation. Model performance and interpretability were assessed using ROC and precision-recall analyses, DeLong's test, permutation testing, SHAP, and permutation importance. Integrative analyses identified 166 candidate genes and prioritized a six-gene signature comprising CGB5, LEP, LIMCH1, LRRC1, PAPPA2, and SIGLEC6. Logistic Regression achieved the highest external performance (ROC-AUC: 0.8516, 95% CI: 0.7913-0.9119; PR-AUC: 0.8572). DeLong's test showed no significant differences from the best-performing deep or hybrid models. Explainability analyses consistently identified LEP, LRRC1, PAPPA2, and SIGLEC6 as major predictive contributors. Exploratory early versus late-onset PE stratification achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.7617. The proposed framework identified a reproducible six-gene placental signature with robust cross-platform predictive performance and biological interpretability. Integrating consensus biomarker selection, external validation, and explainable artificial intelligence may facilitate the reproducible development of transcriptomic biomarkers for precision medicine in PE.

title: Clinician authorization as a safeguard in artificial intelligence-assisted prescribing.
source: PubMed · Polski merkuriusz lekarski : organ Polskiego Towarzystwa Lekarskiego
desc: [Polski merkuriusz lekarski : organ Polskiego Towarzystwa Lekarskiego] Aim: To examine whether clinician authorization is an effective and sufficient safeguard when artificial intelligence influences treatment choices or drug prescribing. Materials and Methods: Purposively selected English-language empirical studies (January 2021 to August 2026; PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, SSRN, and ResearchGate, supplemented by reference lists) were synthesized descriptively alongside a comparative analysis of European Union and United States legislation and guidance. The review does not claim systematic coverage. Generative artificial intelligence was used only to assist source identification and revision. Conclusions: The proposed Meaningful Human Clinical Control test assesses reviewability, competence, time, authority, independent clinical justification, and traceability. These normative domains have no validated scoring method; their purpose is to identify remediable restrictions on clinical review. Liability still depends on the rules on defect, fault, and causation. A signature shows who authorized a prescription, not what that authorization involved.

title: Implementing the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act: Economic and legal impact on the right to healthcare.
source: PubMed · Polski merkuriusz lekarski : organ Polskiego Towarzystwa Lekarskiego
desc: [Polski merkuriusz lekarski : organ Polskiego Towarzystwa Lekarskiego] Aim: To assess the compatibility of the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act with the right to healthcare via the Ukrainian concept of vital security. Materials and Methods: The study was conducted in 2026 and analyzed 29 legal, policy, and academic sources, as well as European Union and Ukrainian legal and policy documents relevant to artificial intelligence in healthcare, fundamental rights, and patient protection. The study applied comparative legal, formal-dogmatic, and systemic-structural methods. Artificial intelligence tools supported information search and proofreading; Grammarly was used for language editing. Conclusions: The European Union Artificial Intelligence Act's market-based risk model contradicts the absolute, "optimizing" approach of a Beveridge healthcare model like Ukraine. To adapt the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, countries should examine artificial intelligence in the medical sphere through fundamental human rights rather than commercial metrics.

title: AI-Driven Clinical Decision Support in Reproductive Medicine: Fertility Oriented Expert (FOX) System.
desc: [Reproductive sciences (Thousand Oaks, Calif.)] Can an AI-driven clinical decision support system reliably support clinical decision making across all steps of assisted reproductive technology (ART) work-up?. This study evaluates Fertility Oriented Expert (FOX), an AI-driven system designed for all steps of ART. FOX incorporates 3,998 full-text, open-access reproductive medicine publications (January 2000 - September 2025) with commercial large language models (LLMs) using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Thirty-two clinical questions covering ART pathway were used to evaluate the system. Responses generated by different FOX models were compared. Three common clinical cases with key diagnostic clues were presented to the FOX-GPT-5 to analyze further if the system could identify these clues and recommend a management plan. Finally, the responses generated by traditional GPT models were compared with the ones generated by FOX. Performance was assessed using G-score and semantic score, with statistical comparison via the Friedman rank-sum. Median G-scores showed no statistically significant differences between the models (0.8 for FOX-GPT-5, 0.8 for FOX-GPT-4o, and 0.95 for FOX-GPT-o1; P = 0.21). Median semantic scores were also similar (0.89 for FOX-GPT-5, 0.89 for FOX-GPT-4o, and 0.9 for FOX-GPT-o1; P = 0.56. For clinical cases, FOX recommended appropriate treatment options, achieving high G-scores and semantic scores (G-score: 1-1; semantic score: 0.88-0.93). GPT models achieved high G-scores and semantic scores based on FOX model answers (G-score: 0.8-1; semantic score: 0.75-0.99) without statistically significant differences between the different GPT models (G-score P = 0.36; semantic score P = 0.65). FOX provides evidence-based information, covering ART pathway, providing clinical decision-making support for fertility specialists.

title: Does access to deep learning uncertainty improve task performance in human readers?
source: PubMed · Journal of medical imaging (Bellingham, Wash.)
desc: [Journal of medical imaging (Bellingham, Wash.)] Deep learning image reconstruction or restoration can produce visually high-quality images that may lack familiar visual cues of reliability. Diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) is a stochastic reconstruction algorithm capable of producing samples from the posterior distribution, offering a potential mechanism to communicate uncertainty and a representation of the posterior distribution to radiologists. We designed and conducted an observer study to evaluate whether displaying multiple DPS posterior samples improves task-based performance in human readers compared with displaying a single DPS sample. The observer study evaluated performance for a binary discrimination task involving spiculated and non-spiculated lung lesions. A total of 200 lung lesions were obtained from the Lung Image Database Consortium dataset, including 100 spiculated and 100 non-spiculated lesions. Computed tomography slices containing these lesions were treated as ground truth. Low-dose projection data were simulated and reconstructed using filtered backprojection and DPS. Six radiologists evaluated each case under four display conditions: low-dose filtered backprojection, a single DPS sample, a scrollable stack of 30 DPS samples, and a tiled display of the same 30 DPS samples. Observer performance was assessed using multi-reader multi-case receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with Lung Image Database Consortium spiculation annotations used as ground truth. Reading time and reader confidence were also recorded. Pooled area under the ROC curves (AUCs) were 0.691 for low-dose filtered-backprojection (FBP), 0.713 for single-sample DPS, 0.750 for the scrollable stack, and 0.747 for the tiled display. Both multi-sample DPS displays improved pooled AUC relative to single-sample DPS at the 10% significance level. The better-performing multi-sample display was reader-dependent. Multi-sample displays were also associated with higher reader confidence than single-sample DPS and FBP displays. Multi-sample displays generally increased reading time, although there was a wide reader-dependent variability in reading time and in which multi-sample display was most time consuming. Averaged over all readers, the scrollable stack and tiled displays increased average reading time by 34.6% and 55.8% relative to low-dose FBP, respectively. Results from the study provide initial evidence that radiologists can use information from multiple posterior samples to improve task-based imaging perform

title: Deep learning inference of plant GRNs at single-cell level: from cis-elements to spatially programmable promoters.
desc: [Journal of experimental botany] Plant regulatory logic emerges from the interaction of cis-regulatory elements, chromatin state, transcription factors, cell identity, and microenvironmental context. This review synthesizes how single-cell and single-nucleus genomics, spatial omics, deep learning, and perturbation frameworks are converging to resolve that logic in plants. We discuss chromatin-first and sequence-informed strategies for discovering candidate cis-regulatory elements, compare major approaches for inferring single-cell gene regulatory networks, and evaluate the promise and limitations of interpretable deep learning and foundation models in data-limited plant systems. We then examine how spatial biology reconnects regulatory inference to tissue geometry, signaling context, and microenvironmental structure, and how perturbation platforms, reporter assays, CRISPRa/i, and programmable promoter engineering can be used to functionally test regulatory predictions. Together, these developments support a transition from descriptive atlases toward iterative design-test-learn frameworks in which candidate elements, networks, and perturbations can be prioritized, validated, and refined across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales.

title: TP-Agent: An Auditable LLM Agent for Predicting Pollutant Transformation Products in Oxidative Water Treatment.
desc: [Environmental science & technology] Predicting the transformation products (TPs) of organic micropollutants is important for characterizing their chemical fate during oxidative water treatment and prioritizing candidate structures for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Limited labeled data and diverse reaction pathways make this task challenging. TP-Agent combines a large language model (LLM), training-only analog retrieval, and executable atom/bond edits to rank TP candidates with inspectable structural records. On 231 standardized-parent-disjoint reactions, TP-Agent achieved 78.8% strict Top-5 accuracy, compared with 65.8% for the bare LLM, 76.2% for standalone retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and 56.3 ± 1.5% for TP-Transformer across three training seeds. Parent-clustered bootstrap analysis supported the gain over the bare LLM; the 2.6-percentage-point difference from RAG was not statistically significant. Retrieval supplied most of the accuracy gain, while graph execution added candidate-linked structural records. Among 1095 candidates, 92.7% had exact edit-replay or deterministic-projection records, measuring structural linkage rather than mechanistic validity. Where available, candidate-linked LLM rationales provide chemical hypotheses for inspection. Estimated parallel latency and API-equivalent cost were 3.5 and 7.4 times those of RAG, respectively. TP-Agent thus combines TP candidate ranking with traceable structural operations and inspectable chemical hypotheses for HRMS follow-up.

title: Cognitive Health and Dementia Care as Nursing Well-Being Policy: Data Linkage, Artificial Intelligence and Illustrative Insights from Japan.
desc: [International nursing review] To clarify cognitive health and dementia care as nursing well-being policy and identify policy levers through which prevention, coordinated care, data linkage and governed artificial intelligence may reduce avoidable nursing burden. Cognitive impairment, dementia and delirium shape nursing work through behavioural crises, fragmented information, repeated documentation, family distress, safety risks and moral strain. Although often treated as clinical or ageing-policy issues, these pressures affect workload, violence exposure, retention and well-being. Japan provides an illustrative context where ageing, dementia reform, community-based care and digital health converge. This non-empirical policy analysis was informed by a targeted narrative evidence synthesis. Searches of nursing and health literature published from January 2014 to May 2026 were supplemented by targeted searches of international and Japanese policy repositories and citation chasing. Sources were prioritised by policy relevance, nursing relevance, evidential strength and applicability. Nursing well-being policy is a focused part of workforce policy addressing workload, safety and moral distress, rather than general employment conditions. Prevention and information continuity may reduce avoidable burden; artificial intelligence remains an adjunct requiring evaluation. Policy levers include education, protected care time, coordination, digital governance and safety culture. Cognitive health and dementia care can support nursing well-being when policies connect prevention, person-centred care, interoperable information and cautious technology governance. Nurses should evaluate cognitive health and dementia initiatives using workload, documentation burden, violence exposure and moral distress. Specify nurse-sensitive measures in dementia-service evaluations, resource prevention and coordination time, and assess documentation and alert burdens when procuring digital tools.

title: FermiLink: An Agent Harness for Multidomain Scientific Simulations.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical theory and computation
desc: [Journal of chemical theory and computation] Artificial intelligence (AI) agent harnesses have been developed for autonomous scientific simulations, but most current agent harnesses are tested on a single or a small set of software packages. Herein, FermiLink, an extensible open-source agent harness, is introduced for multidomain scientific simulations. Its key design principle is the separation of package knowledge bases from simulation workflows, so that simulation workflows in FermiLink, from figure-level simulations to full-paper-level research on high-performance computing clusters, operate uniformly among supported packages via a four-layer progressive disclosure mechanism. This agent harness is specifically optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, enabling multiday, multistep scientific simulations in the absence of human intervention. Using OpenAI Codex as the agent provider, the capabilities of FermiLink are demonstrated across approximately 50 scientific software packages spanning nine research domains from chemistry to engineering. Systematic benchmarks on 132 real-world figure-level reproduction tasks with 44 packages show that FermiLink reproduces 74 (56.1%) of published figures with simulations, among which 30 (22.7%) achieve high-fidelity agreement and 35 reach qualitative agreement with the target figures. A smaller set of human expert-guided reproduction benchmarks with 10 packages in physics and chemistry further highlights the importance of expert insights for improving the simulation fidelity. Beyond reproduction, a single-blinded study demonstrates that FermiLink can produce research-grade results on unpublished polariton physics problems when provided with sufficiently detailed research objectives. Overall, FermiLink provides a scalable research infrastructure that may accelerate the path from scientific questions to computational results across diverse domains.

title: Criminalization of cognitive manipulation and the European Artificial Intelligence Act.
source: PubMed · Polski merkuriusz lekarski : organ Polskiego Towarzystwa Lekarskiego
desc: [Polski merkuriusz lekarski : organ Polskiego Towarzystwa Lekarskiego] Aim: This article aims to highlight the criminal nature of mind manipulation, as emphasised by European bans on the use of artificial intelligence to influence human consciousness. The article seeks to initiate a discussion on the need for innovative changes to doctrinal approaches to criminal law, with the aim of protecting human consciousness from manipulative influences. Materials and Methods: The article addresses issues related to the potential hazardous impact of AI-driven influence on public consciousness, providing an analysis of this phenomenon. Furthermore, it summarises the key provisions of the AI Act relating to the manipulation of consciousness. It summarises the results of judicial practice defined by the keywords 'consciousness manipulation', as well as research into the impact of the internet on the human psyche, particularly that of adolescents, as reported in the media and open sources. Conclusions: It is found that, at the level of national legislation, European states lack norms that would criminalize behavior associated with the manipulation of human consciousness. The need to criminalise the manipulation of consciousness based on the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 5 of the AI Act is substantiated.

title: Teacher-Managed Generative Artificial Intelligence in Undergraduate Chinese and English Literature: Learning Outcomes and Implementation Fidelity.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can support literary explanation and revision, but evaluation requires evidence of independent performance and instructional implementation. This mixed-methods quasi-experimental study compared teacher-managed AI assistance with teacher-led instruction in four intact undergraduate Chinese and English literature sections, with one nonrandomized section per condition within each track. A voluntary, non-credit supplementary module comprised eight 90-min sessions over nine calendar weeks. AI-assisted instruction linked independent annotation, restricted AI assistance, source-text verification, student-authored revision, and teacher checkpoints. Written assessments were supervised without AI. Of 128 baseline participants, 123 provided complete data: 62 AI-assisted and 61 teacher-led students. Literary interpretation, assessed with a 100-point essay rubric, was the primary outcome; secondary outcomes were close reading, course engagement, and self-reported AI critical-use confidence. Exploratory differences adjusted for baseline scores and course track favored AI-assisted instruction by 4.83 points for literary interpretation, 3.65 points for close reading, 0.387 points for engagement, and 0.463 points for confidence. Among AI-assisted complete cases, 62.9% achieved general protocol adherence and 32.3% achieved adequate AI-specific fidelity. Interviews and focus groups with 24 students identified clarification and revision support alongside dependence and authorship concerns. Larger independent performance gains coexisted with incomplete implementation. With only four nonrandomized sections, instructional condition could not be separated from classroom influences; the findings supported exploratory associations and further evaluation of the protocol.

title: Mitigating regional bias in Vietnamese hate speech detection via contrastive learning with adversarial fairness.
desc: [PloS one] Vietnamese hate speech detection (HSD) models can inadvertently latch onto regional dialect cues as spurious shortcuts, producing unfair performance gaps across the country's language varieties. Prior fairness work, however, has largely targeted gender or race in English, and existing Vietnamese HSD resources carry no regional annotation, leaving dialect-driven bias unmeasured. We first construct the Vietnamese Fair Hate Speech Detection dataset (ViFHSD), a dialect-aware corpus of 23,147 comments curated from widely used Vietnamese HSD datasets. Regional labels come from a lexicon of region-specific markers; toxicity labels come from an ensemble large language model (LLM) majority-voting pipeline, validated against native annotators. Building on ViFHSD, we propose Contrastive Learning with Adversarial Fairness (CLAF), which couples a supervised contrastive objective with an adversarial region discriminator and a gradient reversal layer to discourage the predictor from relying on dialect information. Across five pretrained backbones, standard fine-tuning shows large regional disparities, whereas CLAF attains the lowest statistical-parity (ΔSPD) and equal-opportunity (ΔEO) gaps on every backbone, outperforming its adversarial-only and contrastive-only ablations, at a modest macro-F1 cost of 0.6 to 3.2 points. On PhoBERT-v2, for instance, ΔSPD falls from 30.45 to 26.32 and ΔEO from 14.46 to 8.63 for a macro-F1 change of only -0.63. Probing analysis shows these gains arise at the predictor output rather than by erasing dialect information from the representation. Together, ViFHSD and CLAF move Vietnamese HSD toward more regionally consistent moderation within the studied distribution, while making the residual out-of-distribution trade-offs explicit.

title: VGG16-Based Deep Learning for Automated Crack Detection in Solar Panels.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Detection and classification of faults in solar panels are important for maintaining photovoltaic system performance and identifying damaged modules at an early stage. This study proposes a VGG16-based deep learning framework, termed Crack Deep Learning Algorithm (CD-DLA), for automated classification of solar-panel images. The framework extracts discriminative visual features to identify different solar-panel conditions. The study used a Kaggle dataset containing 875 images distributed across six classes: Bird-drop, Clean, Dusty, Electrical-damage, Physical-Damage, and Snow-Covered. The dataset was divided into 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% testing subsets. On the independent held-out test set, the proposed VGG16 model achieved an accuracy of 98.47%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for the evaluated solar-panel condition classification task. However, because the evaluation was performed on a single dataset, further testing on independent datasets is required to assess generalization across different solar-panel types and imaging conditions.

title: MPC-Net: A Physics-Coupled Deep Learning Framework for Boundary Layer Parameterization Correction in Radiation Fog.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
desc: [IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence] Conventional planetary boundary layer (PBL) schemes struggle to capture turbulence structures within foggy boundary layers, leading to significant biases in fog formation and evolution, especially under stable nocturnal conditions and complex terrain. Consequently, such schemes often fail to accurately reproduce the timing, intensity, and spatial distribution of radiation fog. This study proposes a Multiscale Physics-Coupled Correction Network (MPC-Net) that post-processes 3-D atmospheric fields simulated by the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model with conventional PBL schemes. Using a dual-branch heterogeneous network with spatiotemporal attention, MPC-Net learns discrepancies across multiple PBL schemes and their nonlinear mapping to large-eddy simulation (LES) turbulence characteristics. The model separately extracts thermo-dynamic and cloud-phase features, and incorporates physics-informed constraints to improve dynamical consistency. Experimental results show that MPC-Net outperforms conventional schemes, reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) for visibility, liquid water content (LWC), and liquid water path (LWP) by 73.3%, 60.0%, and 66.7%, respectively, over the YSU scheme baseline. The framework improves the spatial reconstruction of fog distribution, temporal stability of fog evolution, and physical consistency in key boundary layer variables. By learning radiation fog physics to correct biases in PBL-scheme outputs, this work offers a new approach for high-resolution fog forecasting.

title: Interference Suppression for Vehicle Platoon Communications Based on Deep Learning Fusion.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Reliable vehicle platoon communication is constrained by fast-varying Doppler channels, co-channel interference among dense sidelink users, and the strict latency requirements of cooperative driving. Existing scheduling, denoising, and reinforcement-learning methods usually optimize either signal recovery or resource allocation, but they seldom represent interference as a link-oriented, control-aware topology. This paper proposes the Deep Learning Fusion based Interference Suppression Network (DLF-ISNet), which integrates a residual complex-signal encoder, a temporal channel-mobility Transformer, a link-centric graph attention encoder, and a gated fusion decision layer. Experiments were conducted on 126,000 simulated cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) sidelink frames under highway, urban-ramp, and mixed-traffic scenarios with 4-12 platoon vehicles and 0-30 external interferers. Across ten independent runs, DLF-ISNet achieved a packet delivery ratio (PDR) of 97.8 ± 0.5%, an average signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of 16.9 ± 0.4 dB, a reported communication delay of 8.6 ± 0.3 ms, and a spacing root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.184 ± 0.012 m. These descriptive simulation comparisons do not establish 10 ms hardware deployment, 99.99% deadline-conditioned reliability, or an architecture-only advantage over baselines with different inputs and objectives.

title: Machine-Learning Dynamics of Redox-Active Materials: Polaron Diffusion on the TiO2(110) Surface.
desc: [ACS nano] In redox-active materials, atoms dynamically change their oxidation states in response to excess charge and electronic transport, with the potential for novel technologies spanning electronics, catalysis, and energy storage and conversion. Despite the remarkable progress of modern artificial intelligence methods in accelerating atomistic simulations, capturing the quantum-mechanical nature of charge transport and dynamically varying oxidation states remains a fundamental challenge, limiting scientific and technological progress. In this work, we introduce a machine-learning-based molecular dynamics framework capable of explicitly tracking the oxidation state dynamics arising from small-polaron hopping (excess charges trapped on single lattice sites that diffuse upon thermal activation). Our model uses descriptors augmented with charge localization information at each time step and is trained on density functional theory data to capture signatures of polaronic diffusion. We apply our method to the rutile TiO2(110) surface, which is a prototypical reducible oxide. Our simulations reveal that charge-carrier diffusion is highly sensitive to the local surface environment: polarons preferentially localize near oxygen vacancies, whereas their interaction with hydroxyl groups is weaker. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of experimental observations, highlight strategies to tune charge-carrier mobility through surface engineering, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach to investigating charge transport in complex materials.

title: AdaptivePy: A Unified Python Framework for Adaptive Sampling in Molecular Dynamics.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical theory and computation
desc: [Journal of chemical theory and computation] Adaptive sampling accelerates the exploration of conformational space in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by repeatedly analyzing the accumulated trajectories and seeding a new round of simulations from informative configurations. A growing collection of adaptive sampling policies has been proposed, each built around a particular notion of what makes a configuration informative, yet these methods are scattered across separate and often incompatible implementations, which complicates their systematic comparison and their combined use in meta-adaptive sampling schemes. Here, we present AdaptivePy, a compact and extensible Python framework that implements nine seed-selection policies behind a single configuration-driven interface, spanning simple population-based baselines, several established machine-learning and geometry-based methods, and two ensemble or meta-sampling policies introduced in this work. We show that the shared implementation reproduces the characteristic selection behavior of each policy on a series of analytic benchmark landscapes. We also introduce a new adaptive sampling scheme that employs TS-DAR, a deep learning framework originally designed to identify transition states, as an acquisition criterion that drives the discovery of an entire multibasin landscape starting from a single basin. We further demonstrate that the common interface enables meta-adaptive sampling policies, which aggregate the rankings of several policies into a single set of seeds. We apply all nine policies to explicit-solvent simulations of alanine dipeptide and the miniprotein chignolin. The policy that performs best depends on the system, on the performance metric, and on the amount of accumulated sampling, justifying the use of meta-policies that combine different algorithms. AdaptivePy thereby provides a unified testbed for the adoption, benchmarking, and continued development of adaptive sampling methods for biomolecular MD simulations.

title: UrbanSeg: Spatial-aware Semantic Segmentation in Urban Scenes.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
desc: [IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence] With the advancement of deep learning, the semantic analysis in 3D urban scenes has gained paramount significance. However, diverse semantic objects in urban scenes take substantial challenges for semantic analysis and limit the practicality in downstream applications. In this paper, we propose a new semantic segmentation method UrbanSegto perceive such complex urban objects. It employs a voxel-based spatial analysis technique to enhance the generalization. Meanwhile, a redesigned spatial-aware network with point-based serialization is utilized in UrbanSeg to improve the perception of various urban objects with different scales and ambiguous geometric relationships. The experiment demonstrates that our method effectively enhances the practicality.
